project: Advanced Programming 2026 — Question 2: Monte Carlo pricing and hedging on Chinese futures
seed_note: Data retrieval is deterministic given the AKShare endpoints; no randomness involved.

if_main.csv.series: CSI 300 stock-index futures, IF main continuous contract (IF0)
if_main.csv.roll_convention: AKShare 'main contract' continuous series; rolls on dominant open-interest/volume contract; artificial roll gaps possible in levels, mitigated by modelling log returns and disclosing the convention.
if_main.csv.units: index points (CNY per point × 300 per contract)

shibor.csv.provider: AKShare (ak.macro_china_shibor_all) → China Foreign Exchange Trade System / Eastmoney mirror
shibor.csv.series: Shanghai Interbank Offered Rate fixings, all tenors, daily
shibor.csv.units: percent per annum (e.g. 1.44 == 1.44%); converted to decimals in code

estimation_window.calibration_note: Downstream scripts estimate μ, σ on trailing 5 calendar years of the retrieved history unless overridden; the window is stated in results/*/metrics.json.

missing_data_policy: Rows with non-numeric or missing close are dropped; SHIBOR fixings are forward/back-filled only for curve interpolation, never for return estimation. Gaps (e.g. 2015-05 tabulated row) are reported by fetch.py --refresh.
transformations: prices cast to float64; volumes to float64
SHIBOR percent → decimal fraction only inside pricing code (r = y1 / 100)
